header: Hyperconjugation and Its Applications to Structure and Reactivity

subquestions.text_open: 8.1 The molecule shown below can undergo intramolecular alkylation with the carbonyl oxygen acting as the nucleophile, forming 2 possible salt products. For this transformation, determine which reaction pathway is preferred and write the SMILES representation of the salt product corresponding to that pathway.
8.2 Only one stereochemical configuration of the molecule shown below can react effectively with $O_3$. Write the SMILES representation of the reactive stereochemical configuration.

8.3 $N_2F_2$ has 2 stereoisomers. Determine which is thermodynamically more stable and which is kinetically more reactive, and explain the origin of the greater thermodynamic stability. (No more than 100 words.)
8.4 Which of the following conformations is more stable?

text_images.description: Both molecules have the SMILES representation 'O=P(O[R]C)(O[R])[O-]' but differ in conformation. Structure A: the central P atom is bonded to =O directly below and to $-O^-$ at the upper left. Of the two -O-R groups bonded at the upper right, one P-O bond points into the plane of the page, with the R group on its oxygen extending vertically upward, while the other P-O bond points out of the plane, with the R group on its oxygen extending down and to the right. Structure B: the connectivity between P and the four oxygen atoms is the same as in structure A. For the -OR group at the upper right of P that points into the plane, the R group lies below and to the left of O and points into the plane; for the -OR group at the upper right of P that points into the plane, the R group lies below and to the left of O and points out of the plane. The overall difference from A is the positions of the R groups.
